quiz.question: Which data structure efficiently handles 2D proximity searches for location-based queries?
options: Hash Table with composite keys derived from latitude and longitude pairs
quiz.explanation: Geospatial indexes (geohashes, quadtrees, R-trees) organise points by location so nearby users can be found without a full scan.

quiz.question: Why must recording a swipe and checking for a reciprocal swipe be atomic?
options: Otherwise two simultaneous right-swipes could both miss each other and the match is never created
To make the feed load faster
quiz.explanation: Without atomicity, each request can check before the other's write lands, so neither sees the match.

quiz.question: What is the main trade-off of using a Bloom filter to avoid showing repeat profiles?
options: Occasional false positives (a profile is wrongly hidden)
It needs a full table scan
It can't be stored in memory
quiz.explanation: Bloom filters never miss a seen profile but may occasionally report an unseen one as seen — usually acceptable here.

quiz.question: Why is Redis a good fit for swipe matching?
options: Its atomic operations make check-and-set on swipes consistent and fast
It stores data only on disk
quiz.explanation: Keeping both users' swipes under one key lets a single atomic operation record a swipe and detect the match.
